column8: Thu 19 Nov: store, background for row 36's comparison (the shipping trade's firm point is subjects lifted, a declaration); Baltic Code wording re-read at source by the rater; never map Laura's top to on subjects, since either side may walk away and IPS l.15 fixes the move.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c or 3d, one clause behind pencil at most, read cold with the definition first (the cargo is there before the ship is fixed, the Treasury is owned before the figure is stated); the Code's wording re-read at source by the rater, but the etymology may be a backronym, so say the Baltic Exchange's guide says; never subject to stem said of Laura.

Thu 19 Nov: store, the real case behind row 2; Trafigura could walk away and Laura cannot (IPS l.15, l.17), so it supports the STEM clause and never stands as a parallel of its own; never Laura can fail her top.

Thu 19 Nov: twin of row 1 (pencil means no contract), read only as quoted; its 3d use misleads twice: abeyance reads Laura's pencil as undecided (V2.5, Q114's refused rows) and it implies her ink gives co-sponsors a claim, when her Treasuries are held for her and co-sponsors hold nothing (Q72).

Thu 19 Nov: 3d store, a court's reason for a clean line between pencil and ink (the other side can plan), behind the line before Laura's words at most; cite as [1988] 2 Lloyd's Rep 583 from the Nautica judgment, never the law firm's 1958.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c store behind why nothing is stated before the move (NUMBERS 4: the move would buy less than a top stated a year early in about 11 of 100, 10.6%, matches); needs demurrage explained, so Boeing (row 25) does the same job more plainly; secured stays on Nautica's side, never Laura's (Q147).

Thu 19 Nov: 3d, re-read at source by the rater: the Baltic Code calls holding a vessel on subjects to judge market direction abuse; fix the mapping before use: Laura's top moves with shares until a dated move, never she waits for the market (no market timing, IPS l.15 and l.17); she holds no co-sponsor on pencil because she states nothing before the move.
Thu 19 Nov: the same abuse in trade press (undated, no author, no frequency); row 7's Code rule carries it at source.

Thu 19 Nov: subject to board approval means no contract in English shipping law; for co-sponsors' own pledges Q83's Taiwan rows (art. 408, board minutes) are closer to the residency; never a dig at co-sponsors in Laura's words.

Thu 19 Nov: same job as Q141-027 (Laura's pencil is decided and dated, not undecided), but neither legal category fits by the card's own account, so chart pencil carries it more plainly; writers' note only.

Thu 19 Nov: process guard only, serves no part: The Merak is an incorporation case (arbitration clause in the bills of lading, Scarman J, 28 Jul 1964, proceedings stayed), checked at the CMI database by the rater; never cite it for when a fixture binds.

Thu 19 Nov: writers' disanalogy for 2.0 (the law's ink means decided, Laura's means owned, and owning cannot be agreed into being), the V2.5 disanalogy already recorded from Q114 with a crisp quote; read only as quoted, never a turn.

Thu 19 Nov: support for row 36 (a binding ship sale needed neither signature nor deposit), read through a law firm's circular, not the report; one of the facts that kills the card's claim 1 as worded.
Thu 19 Nov: support for row 36 (a ship sale's money down is a tenth); deposits secure a sale, Laura's Treasuries pay the figure itself, so a comparison of standards only.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d, one clause behind pencil (re-read at source by the rater: s. 6.4 defines Pencil Booking, s. 6.9 a signed agreement and deposit); move it from 2.0, since round 7 found naming signed beside the definition costs it; a venue pencil is a queue place, not a dollar figure; Australia only if Caplet finds it earns its place.
Thu 19 Nov: store, disanalogy only: a venue pencil turns to ink or erasure on a rival's challenge, Laura's on dates fixed in advance; never a trigger (IPS l.17).
Thu 19 Nov: 3d store, the venue wording nearest Laura's rule (wanting a date is not confirming it); still signed and part-paid, so support for row 36's comparison.
Thu 19 Nov: store, support for row 37 (holds are free and bind no one, so the venue carries pencil's cost; confirming is half down).
Thu 19 Nov: store, the one 100% case behind row 36's exception; money paid away, Laura's owned and earning.
Thu 19 Nov: another venue's ladder of firmness (confirmed means signed); the Opera House's defined term is the stronger venue fact.

Thu 19 Nov: 3.0 fact behind certainty has dates (the money is whole only near the date; most of each of Laura's payments is inked six years ahead, at least about $42,000 of each $50,000 even at zero, NUMBERS 8h, matches CONCEIT 3.0); say one stadium's rule, never the trades; never all ten fully inked in January 2027; competes with Image's three completed issues, one turn per part.
Thu 19 Nov: pencil as a ranked word in live events (UK promoters, a New Zealand venue); the Opera House's defined Pencil Booking does the same job at source.
Thu 19 Nov: 3d store and support for row 37: in casting the performer keeps its diary free on a pencil; an agency blog, so cite only as the trade's usage.
Thu 19 Nov: the same performer's-side point; pay-or-play is a promise to pay (owed, Q72), no author or date, and the word is on row 39's guard list.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c aha, one clause behind nothing is stated before the move, re-read at source by the rater (10-K backlog: contingencies must clear even if satisfying such conditions is highly probable); NUMBERS 4's 10.6% matches; drop the world's largest aircraft order book (not on the card's sources, and Airbus's backlog is larger), say Boeing's; Boeing's next test is probability, so never Laura's rule is accounting practice; near Q106-019.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d support for row 25, figures re-read at source by the rater ($17,759m net ASC 606 adjustments, $11,094m cancellations, BCA backlog $567,290m); fix: label the 3.1% as of the year-end backlog (4.1% of the start-year $435,175m), say payment or commitment in doubt (sanctions among them), keep it out of 2.0 (signed beside the definition) and never backed as the meaning of ink.
Thu 19 Nov: the same 10-K backlog section (options and unexecuted orders excluded, re-read by the rater); progress payments add nothing row 21 does not.
Thu 19 Nov: store, the nearest trade rule to Laura's (final when usable funds are received); within finance, so not dissimilar; it also bounds row 36: never her rule is stricter than any trade.
Thu 19 Nov: the charge-back half of the same UCC Article 4 rule; carry it with row 28 if used, never nothing can be taken back without the fund-cost limit beside it.
Thu 19 Nov: 2.5 writers' guard: the click made the order irrevocable, the bond was hers only at settlement, so a click is ink stays a passing word and never says the click itself made the bond hers.
Thu 19 Nov: agreed, bound, owned; Q79-004's register entry does the 2.0 job closer to the residency's country, as the card says; never name signed beside the definition.
Thu 19 Nov: the order of claims in a newspaper's layout; Q79-036 and H7-015 carry the order of claims, and staged it would be a second trade image.
Thu 19 Nov: store only; the parallel breaks under its own disanalogy (her flexibility is never taken by anyone, only unpromised) and the price premium is unverified; never staged.
Thu 19 Nov: store only; firming is the airline's verb for pencil to ink, but ticketing is payment for a service and the page is deactivated; never firm or firming as the meaning of ink (row 39).

Thu 19 Nov: 3d or 3e store: a builder's standard form lets the contractor ask the owner for evidence of funds, money not promises; a US form, so never imply Taiwan's builders use it (the case leaves Taiwan law out); A201's clause unread.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d, the card's main finding and the right correction of claim 1, false as worded (the trades go firm on being bound): Laura's rule for stating a figure is stricter than a shipowner's, a theatre's, a house buyer's or Boeing's; fix: often, not usually, part of the money down (charters and Blankenstein take none); never stricter than any trade (bank final payment also needs the money in hand, row 28); not at 2.0, where round 7 keeps signed away from the definition.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d, a fresh reason for stating nothing before the move: in the trades read the side holding a ship, a date or a diary carries pencil's risk, while Laura carries her own (before the move a fall lands on her top and flexibility, NUMBERS 8p); keep the one limit co-sponsors share beside it (fund costs beyond the fee past the room under the top); Poseidon's quote is unchecked by the rater.
Thu 19 Nov: writers' note for 27 Nov: these facts go behind working words, never staged (rounds 6-8); STEM, the Opera House and Boeing are the three to read cold, one per part at most.
Thu 19 Nov: guard list, consistent with CONCEIT V2.4 guards 3-4 and Q147 (never secured); keeps owned as ink's meaning while the trade facts are used.
